457	## Keys: `keys.json`
458	
459	```json
460	{
461	  "global":   { "ctrl-shift-t": "tab.new", "ctrl-shift-o": "pane.split:right", "alt-1": "space.select:1" },
462	  "terminal": { "ctrl-shift-c": "terminal.copy", "ctrl-left": "send:\u001bb", "ctrl-1": "terminal" },
463	  "layout:terminals": { "ctrl-shift-pagedown": "space.next", "ctrl-shift-pageup": "space.prev" },
464	  "mod:editor": { "ctrl-s": "editor.save" }
465	}
466	```
467	
468	- Sections: `global`, `layout:<name>` (while `layouts/<name>.json` shows),
469	  `terminal` (a terminal has focus), `mod:<name>`. The more specific section
470	  wins: `layout:terminals` over `global`, `terminal` over both.
471	- An action is a command (`name`, or `name:value`: the value fills the
472	  command's first argument), `send:<text>` (types into the terminal),
473	  `<mod>.<command>` (delivered to that mod's `nextCommand()`), or `terminal`
474	  (the program gets the key).
475	- Plain ctrl+letters go to the program unless bound. Programs rely on
476	  ctrl+c, ctrl+d, ctrl+l, ctrl+r, ctrl+w, ctrl+a, ctrl+e, ctrl+u, ctrl+k,
477	  ctrl+z and ctrl+[ (Escape); ctrl+alt is AltGr on Windows; option+digits
478	  and letters type characters on many Mac keyboards (`[`, `@`). Don't pick
479	  these on your own. If the person asks for one, bind it and tell them what
480	  it takes from typing.
481	- Windows AltGr and dead-key compositions type text in terminals. macOS
482	  dead keys compose accents through native text input; Option keeps its
483	  keyboard-layout characters rather than acting as Alt.
484	- Terminal keys honor the program's negotiated Kitty mode, including on Windows.
485	
486	## Commands
487	
488	The one way to change anything; keys, mods (`run(name, args)`), menus and
489	you use the same list. `herdr-app commands` prints every one with its arguments
490	(which are required) and what it does. Unknown argument names are errors and list
491	valid names; they never fall back to the current target. For example, closing a
492	space uses `herdr-app do space.close --id <id> --confirmed true`, not `--space`.
493	The main ones:
494	
495	- Spaces: `space.new {name?, folder?, tab?, argv?, task?, machine?}`
496	  (machine: another machine from `hc machine ls`; the space lives there, its
497	  terminals start in that machine's home unless folder, and its tabs and
498	  splits stay there; `spaces()` gives each space's `machine`, null here),
499	  `space.close {id?, confirmed?}`, `space.rename {id?, name}` ("": Herdr's name again),
500	  `space.move {id, index}`, `space.select {index | id}`, `space.next`, `space.prev`.
501	  With no `argv`, the target core chooses that machine's default shell (PowerShell 7 when available on Windows).
502	- Tabs: `tab.new {name?, space?, folder?, argv?, task?}` (argv: an
503	  agent to run, task: its first message). Agents run in your interactive
504	  shell (including fish), which stays open after the agent exits. A terminal
505	  that exits with a nonzero code within two seconds of launch shows an error
506	  toast with its exit code and last output lines. Or `tab.new {name?, space?, mod,
507	  props?}` for a tab whose only pane is a mod (a file, a board; split a shell
508	  in beside it like any tab), `tab.close {id?, confirmed?}` (closing the last tab
509	  closes its space and asks first unless confirmed),
510	  `tab.rename {id?, name}` ("": its number again), `tab.move {id, index}`,
511	  `tab.select {index | id}`, `tab.next`, `tab.prev`,
512	  `tab.settle {id?}`, `tab.unsettle {id?}` (index, next and prev
513	  skip settled tabs).
514	- Panes: `pane.split {direction: "right" | "down", pane?, argv? | mod?, props?}` (a new
515	  terminal, or a mod pane), `pane.close {pane?}`,
516	  `pane.zoom {pane?}`, `pane.focus {pane | terminal}`, `pane.go {direction}`, `pane.swap {direction}`.
517	  `pane.focus {terminal}` prefers the first visible layout terminal block showing that
518	  address, then its model pane. Clicking a terminal block focuses it too.
519	  While a layout terminal block is focused, implicit split/close/zoom/go/swap and
520	  `terminal.show` fail, as do `terminal.open`/`terminal.keep` with place right/down.
521	  They never act on the terminal's source pane. An explicit `pane` still targets that
522	  model pane; composition edits belong to the mod (edit its layout instead).
523	- Terminals: `terminal.open {argv?, folder?, place?, name?}`, `terminal.kill {terminal}`,
524	  `terminal.keep {terminal, place?}`, `terminal.park {terminal}`,
525	  `terminal.peek {terminal}` (peek over the tab, with keep-as-tab and close),
526	  `terminal.show {terminal?, pane?}`, `terminal.copy`, `terminal.paste` (an image
527	  alone, into a terminal on another machine: copied there, its path pasted; a
528	  local program reads the clipboard itself), `terminal.paste_image` (Ctrl+V: the
529	  same for an image; otherwise Ctrl+V goes to the program). TIFF and BMP clipboard
530	  images are converted to PNG before sending,
531	  `terminal.right_click {to: "program" | "menu", terminal?}` (where right-clicks go
532	  when the program takes the mouse; kept as its label `herdr.right-click=program`;
533	  Shift+right-click is always Herdr's menu). Copy, paste, paste-image and implicit
534	  right-click targeting follow keyboard focus, including peek and floating terminals;
535	  with no terminal holding keyboard focus, they use the focused pane or block.
536	- Agents: `agent.next`, `agent.prev`, `agent.focus {terminal}`.
537	- Layout: `layout.switch {name?}`, `layout.toggle {id}`, `layout.show {id}`, `layout.hide {id}`,
538	  `layout.resize {id, px | weight}`, `layout.select {stack, child}`, `layout.set {layout}`
539	  (personal tree edits; on shipped layouts only click/look fields change),
540	  `layout.reset {name?}` (reset a shipped layout and its clicks),
541	  `layout.clone {name, as?}` (duplicate, then switch; default `<name>-copy`).
542	- App: `mod.clone {name, as?}` (duplicate; default `<name>-copy`), `mod.open {name}`, `overlay.close {id?}`, `app.help`, `app.palette`, `app.settings {section?}`
543	  (sections: `look`, `machines`, `alerts`, `updates`, `privacy`; Machines lists, updates, renames and removes ssh machines; settings edit the same files you do),
544	  `app.check_updates`, `app.update_core` (a newer herdr-core of this generation, terminals kept;
545	  never one a package manager owns), `app.welcome`, `app.whats_new`, `app.feedback {message?, from?}` (from `"person"` or `"agent"`; opens a review window, where the person can paste up to 3 screenshots; never sends until the person clicks Send), `app.reset`,
546	  `app.theme {name}`, `app.zoom_in`, `app.zoom_out`, `app.zoom_reset`,
547	  `app.update` (restart into a downloaded update).
548	- Window: `window.minimize`, `window.maximize` (or back), `window.close`.
549	- macOS: `app.quit`, `app.hide`, `app.hide_others`, `app.show_all`.
550	
551	When the user runs a command without a required name (a key, a click), Herdr
552	asks them. **You never get a dialog**: pass every required argument, or the
553	command says what's missing.
554	
555	From a shell:
556	
557	```sh
558	herdr-app do tab.new --name "fix login" --argv '["claude"]' --task "look at the login bug"
559	herdr-app do pane.split:right
560	herdr-app ls          # spaces, their tabs and terminals (sub-agents under their parent)
561	herdr-app status      # what's on screen: layout, focus, overlays, zoom, errors from files and mods
562	herdr-app commands    # every command and its arguments
563	```
564	
565	`herdr-app do` prints what the command made (`{ "space", "tab",
566	"terminal" }`, `{ "pane", "terminal" }`) or `{ "error": "..." }` and exits 1.

568	## The person: `settings.json`
569	
570	What's about the user, never a look:
571	
572	```json
573	{ "zoom": 1, "sounds": { "enabled": true } }
574	```
575	
576	- `zoom` scales the whole app: terminals, mods, the layout's px sizes
577	  (0.5 to 3; the zoom keys change it). Write sizes as designed at zoom 1.
578	- `sounds`: `{ "enabled": true, "done": "<file>", "blocked": "<file>" }`.
579	  When an agent needs the person, or finishes while they aren't looking at
580	  it, Herdr plays a sound and (unless they're looking) posts a toast that
581	  goes there when clicked. `done` / `blocked` replace the bundled MP3s
582	  (path absolute or relative to `~/.config/herdr-app`).
583	- `core`: the herdr-core binary to use, when it isn't where Herdr looks
584	  (PATH, the login shell's PATH, `~/.local/bin`, Homebrew, mise, Nix,
585	  cargo). Read at start.
586	- `font`, `font_size`, `ui_font`: used where the layout doesn't set its
587	  own. Herdr (main) leaves these unset. Bigger panels: `zoom`.
588	- `theme`: a theme name or `{light, dark}`; used where the layout sets none.
589	  The theme picker overrides any layout and stays on that layout.
590	- `colors`: theme color overrides (`{"accent":"#ff8800"}`), with the same
591	  precedence as fonts.
592	- `appearance`: `"light"` or `"dark"` always; absent, the system's. A layout
593	  with a light and a dark theme shows the matching one.
594	- Updates: an installed app downloads them by itself and offers Restart and
595	  What changed. If the app crashes or is killed with a verified newer update
596	  waiting, the next launch installs it before opening a window. The first
597	  start after an app update also updates herdr-core
598	  to the latest release of the same generation, keeping terminals running.
599	  Settings → Updates keeps app and core actions together;
600	  its What's new button opens the waiting update's release range, or this
601	  version's notes, in the What's new window. Reading never clears the waiting-update dot.
602	  Rare spotlight releases open What’s new after restart, once; otherwise a
603	  quiet Updated pill lasts for that launch. A build from source never updates.
604	  Curated notes come from the bundled root `CHANGELOG.md`; remote notes and
605	  media are optional. `update-notes.json` records the last successful app
606	  version and presented spotlights; `update-notes-cache.md` caches remote
607	  notes; `update-notes-media/` caches HTTPS images (including animated WebP clips),
608	  referenced below its item in the changelog as `![label](https://...)`.
609	  Each version uses `### New` with `- **Headline.** detail` highlights and
610	  `### Fixed` with short bullet items. Unsectioned bullets are plain items.
611	  Notes expose `items` with `headline`, `detail`, `fixed`, and cached `media`
612	  objects (`path`, pixel `width`, pixel `height`). Highlights use matching cards:
613	  edge-to-edge media at its original aspect ratio, then headline and detail.
614	  For local release-media previews only, launch with
615	  `HERDR_NOTES_MEDIA_DIR=/var/tmp/herdr-notes-media`: URLs under
616	  `https://media.herdr.dev/<version>/<scene>.webp` use that directory's
617	  `<version>/<scene>.webp` instead of downloading. Without the variable,
618	  media uses the normal HTTPS cache.
619	  Mods use `updates().notes` and `presentUpdateNotes([version])` only
620	  for spotlight entries actually shown expanded, not collapsed headlines.
621	  macOS releases require Apple Silicon; Intel Macs must build from source.
622	  Keep signed macOS bundles unchanged: don't edit their Info.plist or
623	  re-sign them. On launch, an installed macOS bundle creates or repairs its
624	  own `~/.local/bin/herdr-app` symlink, leaving personal files and other
625	  apps' links alone. Disk-image and translocated launches don't create it.
626	  Finder launches load the login shell's PATH, with the usual install
627	  folders as a fallback.
628	- `option_as_alt`: macOS only, `"auto"` (default), `"on"`, or `"off"`.
629	  `"auto"` sends Option as Alt on US, US International, ABC and ABC variants;
630	  other layouts keep native Option text and dead keys. `"on"` enables terminal
631	  Alt shortcuts (including Option+E without composition); `"off"` keeps native
632	  Option input on every layout. Changes apply immediately, including layout
633	  switches. Linux and Windows are unchanged.
634	- `minimum_contrast`: terminal text contrast ratio, `1` (default) leaves
635	  program colors unchanged. Set it to `1.6` to enable the previous readability
636	  adjustment, or another number from `1` to `21`. Text below that ratio is
637	  replaced with near-white or near-black, whichever contrasts more with its
638	  background; this is a threshold, not a guaranteed resulting ratio.
639	  Box/block, Powerline and sprite glyph colors are never adjusted.
640	  Changes apply immediately, including text already on screen.
641	- `clipboard_write`: `false` blocks terminal programs from writing the local
642	  clipboard (default `true`, including remote terminals attached in this window).
643	  OSC 52 accepts base64 UTF-8 text up to 1 MiB: `c` writes the system clipboard,
644	  `p` writes Linux primary selection. `s` is ignored; cut buffers `0`–`7`
645	  are treated as the system clipboard.
646	  Clipboard reads (`?`) are never allowed.
647	- `telemetry`: `false` stops anonymous usage data and deletes what wasn't
648	  sent (on when absent; Settings → Privacy shows each report word for
649	  word, and `telemetry()` in mods). Once a day the app sends counts:
650	  version, OS, which known agents ran, how many spaces, tabs and
651	  terminals, which layouts, shipped mods and commands were used. Never
652	  terminal content, names of files, folders, spaces or the person's own
653	  mods; nothing from herdr-core. `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` or `HERDR_TELEMETRY=0`
654	  turns it off for one run. A build from source never sends.
655	
656	## Programs: `programs.json`
657	
658	Every pane, agent and terminal carries `program`: its name, icon and tile,
659	from one table, so every mod shows the same. An agent's own report wins;
660	else the program the terminal runs (an interpreter shows what it runs:
661	`node .../vite` is Vite, `npx vitest` is Vitest); shells are `shell`,
662	anything unlisted is `program` with a color of its own. The built-in table
663	has 120 programs (agents, editors, runtimes, tools, databases, infra);
664	`programs.json` here adds to it or changes entries field by field:
665	
666	```json
667	{ "programs": {
668	    "lazygit": { "name": "Git", "tile": "#f05032" },
669	    "mytool": { "name": "My Tool", "icon": "my-icons/mytool.svg", "tint": true,
670	                "tile": "#334155", "color": "#ffffff", "match": ["mytool-dev"] } },
671	  "shells": ["xonsh"], "interpreters": ["pipx"] }
672	```
673	
674	- `icon`: a path in the home folder. `tint: true` for a one-color glyph
675	  (drawn in `color` on a tile, or the text color), false for a picture.
676	- `match`: other process names (or agents' `app` names) for the entry.
677	- `run`: how to start it (`["cursor-agent"]`), for agents people start
678	  from a menu: `knownAgents()` lists the entries with one, and whether this
679	  machine (or another) has them installed. For example, override
680	  `"claude": { "run": ["my-claude"] }` or add
681	  `"claude-alt": { "name": "Claude (alt)", "icon": "icons/claude.svg", "run": ["my-claude-alt"] }`
682	  inside `programs`. Use programs or shell functions, not aliases (the launcher
683	  does not expand them). Local checks include functions in shells such as bash
684	  and zsh; fish and remote checks find executables only. Installation
685	  checks are cached for up to a minute; changing the commands checks again.
686	  Invalid JSON is reported in `programs.error` (a valid file has no error).
687	- It follows what runs in the terminal now (lazygit, nvim), else what it
688	  started with.
689	
690	## Mods: `mods/<name>/`
691	
692	```
693	~/.config/herdr-app/mods/<name>/
694	  main.js       the mod (required)
695	  mod.json    where it first appears: { "place": "right" | "left" | "top" | "bottom" | "none", "size": 320 }
696	  *.js, *.svg   more modules ("./ui.js"), its own icons
697	```
698	
699	- The first time Herdr sees a folder, it docks one copy per `mod.json` into
700	  the shown layout (`"none"`: only where a layout or another mod puts it).
701	  After that, the layouts decide. Saving any file reloads every copy in place
702	  (not files the app writes: `jsconfig.json`, `.d.ts`, hidden ones,
703	  `node_modules`). The old build's tasks and timers stop: a loop ends at its
704	  next `cx` use. A broken save keeps the old version running and shows in
705	  `herdr-app status`; its top-level code has already run, so keep side effects
706	  on `globalThis` out of the module's top level.
707	- A copy starts the first time it shows, then stays alive while its block is in
708	  the layout, shown or not (a hidden column, the other child of a stack, a pane
709	  in another tab or behind a zoom): switching back finds it as it was. Its
710	  timers keep running while hidden, so poll gently. Another layout starts its
711	  mods fresh (pane mods belong to their tab and stay); a block removed or given
712	  another mod or props starts over. `<mod>.<command>` reaches shown copies only.
713	- Images and SVGs are referenced from `~/.config/herdr-app`:
714	  `image("mods/<name>/logo.svg")` (full color), `svg("mods/<name>/icon.svg")`
715	  (tinted with the text color).
716	- The defaults are mods too, read them as examples: `spaces`, `agents`,
717	  `tabs` (the tab bar), `menu`, `prompt`, `confirm`, `help`, `toast`,
718	  Terminals' `picker`, `peek`, and `pane` (an
719	  example pane header, not used by the default layouts), and `worktree`
720	  (git worktrees as spaces: the space menu's and the + menu's New worktree,
721	  Open worktree (the repo's checkouts, filtered; one already shown is gone
722	  to) and Remove worktree open it as a dialog with props `{space, folder?,
723	  action: "new" | "open" | "remove"}` (the repo: folder, else where the
724	  space's first terminal is), or with `{branch, tab?, argv?}` to make one at once with
725	  that first tab; checkouts go to
726	  `~/.herdr/worktrees/<repo>/<branch>` on the space's machine, a constant
727	  at its top; the
728	  `spaces` sidebar nests worktree spaces under their repo's and shows each
729	  space's repo, branch, ahead/behind and uncommitted changes). Shipped mods
730	  are Herdr's; duplicate with `mod.clone` before editing.
731	
732	### Check before you finish
733	
734	```sh
735	herdr-app check ~/.config/herdr-app/mods/<name>
736	```
737	
738	Loads the mod, renders it once, exits nonzero with the exact error. Run it
739	after every change. Never call a mod done without a passing check.
740	
741	### A mod
742	
743	```js
744	import { View, div } from "gpui-kit";
745	import { v_flex, h_flex } from "gpui-base";
746	import { exec, spaces, theme, run } from "herdr";
747	
748	export default class Branches extends View {
749	  init(_props, cx) {
750	    this.branch = {};
751	    cx.timer.every(3000, (cx) => this.refresh(cx));
752	    this.refresh(cx);
753	  }
754	
755	  refresh(cx) {
756	    cx.spawn(async (cx) => {
757	      for (const p of spaces()) {
758	        // on: a space on another machine runs git there.
759	        const r = await exec("git", ["branch", "--show-current"], { cwd: p.folder, on: p.machine });
760	        this.branch[p.id] = r.stdout.trim();
761	      }
762	      cx.notify();
763	    });
764	  }
765	
766	  render(cx) {
767	    const t = theme();
768	    return v_flex().size_full().bg(t.surface).p(10).gap(4).text_size(13).children(
769	      spaces().map((p) =>
770	        h_flex().id(`b-${p.id}`).gap(8).hover((s) => s.bg(t.raised))
771	          .on_click(() => run("space.select", { id: p.id }))
772	          .child(div().text_color(p.active ? t.foreground : t.muted).child(p.name))
773	          .child(div().text_color(t.dim).child(this.branch[p.id] ?? ""))));
774	  }
775	}
776	```
777	
778	Rules:
779	- `main.js` default-exports a class extending `View`. `init(props, cx)` runs
780	  once; `render(cx)` describes the UI and runs again after `cx.notify()` and
781	  whenever Herdr's live data changes (spaces, agents, terminals, focus,
782	  theme, shared state). Don't poll those.
783	- **Never keep a `cx` and use it later.** Every callback gets its own:
784	  `on_click((event, cx) => …)`, `cx.spawn(async (cx) => …)`,
785	  `cx.timer.every(ms, (cx) => …)`.
786	- No `setTimeout`/`setInterval` (use `cx.timer`), no top-level `await` (use
787	  `cx.spawn` in `init`). Anything slow goes through `exec` or `fetch`.
788	- Size: put `.id("root").on_size_change((size, cx) => { this.size = size; cx.notify(); })`
789	  on the root `div()`, `h_flex()` or `v_flex()`. It reports `{width, height}`
790	  in logical pixels after the first layout and whenever the size changes,
791	  even with the pointer elsewhere. It does not change `props()`.
792	- Cleanup: an optional `async close(cx)` on the exported `View` gets one final
793	  call when its pane, tab, layout-owned slot or overlay goes, and on app quit.
794	  It is not called for a hidden copy or an inactive tab. Start cleanup inside
795	  `close()`; don't await work started earlier. Await cleanup directly,
796	  for example `async close(cx) { await exec("hc", ["kill", this.browser]); }`.
797	  Closing stays responsive: cleanup has at most 250 ms (shared across copies
798	  on quit), then unfinished tasks are cancelled. On quit, use `exec(...)` and
799	  `run("terminal.kill", { terminal: address })`: those go out before the event
800	  loop stops; other commands may not run. An `exec` already started keeps
801	  running; don't start new long-lived work in `close`. This is best-effort,
802	  not a guarantee after a crash or forced termination.
803	- Use `theme()` colors so the mod follows the user's theme.
804	- **Animate natively, never with a timer.** Every redraw of a mod redraws
805	  the whole window, so `cx.timer.every(90, () => cx.notify())` for a
806	  spinner costs real battery. Use `.frames(["⠋", "⠙", …], 90)` (shows
807	  each string in turn as the element's text), `svg(arc).spin(900)` (turns
808	  an icon once every 900 ms: a ring spinner, e.g.
809	  `mods/workspace-chrome/spinner.svg`), or `.loop("opacity", { from:
810	  0.4, to: 1, period: 1200 })` (also width, height, left, top), and
811	  `.transition(...)` for changes: they run without your script and stop
812	  when not shown. Timers are for data (a clock, a fetch), and only as often
813	  as what they show changes.
814	
815	### UI
816	
817	Chained builders with GPUI's snake_case names: `div()`, `h_flex()`,
818	`v_flex()`; `.size_full()`, `.flex_1()`, `.gap(n)`, `.p(n)`, `.px(n)`,
819	`.w(n)`, `.h(n)`, `.items_center()`, `.justify_between()`,
820	`.overflow_y_scrollbar()`; `.child("text")`, `.text_size(n)`, `.font_semibold()`,
821	`.truncate()`, `.text_color(c)`; `.bg(c)`, `.border(1)`, `.border_color(c)`,
822	`.rounded(n)`; `.id("unique")` then `.on_click(...)`, `.on_mouse_down("right", ...)`,
823	`.hover((s) => s.bg(c))`, `.on_scroll_wheel(...)`; keyboard: `this.h = cx.focus_handle()`
824	in init, `.track_focus(this.h).on_key_down((e, cx) => …)`, `this.h.focus()`.
825	`.on_drop((event, cx) => …)` on a plain layout element receives external files as
826	`event.paths` (absolute paths). The feedback form accepts dropped images with
827	the same limits, previews and removal as picked images.
828	`.on_hover((hovered, cx) => …)` reports pointer entry and exit on buttons
829	and other interactive controls too.
830	`.when(cond, (el) => …)`, `.children([...])`. Controls from `gpui-base`
831	(`Button`, `Checkbox`, `Switch`, `InputState` + `Input`) are unstyled: style
832	them. Text: `TextView.markdown(id, text)` renders markdown; `EditorState.new({
833	language, value, readonly, font_family: settings().font_family, syntax: {
834	keyword: theme().ansi5, ... } })` + `Editor.new(state)` is a code view (readonly)
835	or editor with syntax highlighting, line numbers and folding. A viewer opens
836	beside the shell as a pane: `pane.split {direction, mod, props: { file }}`.
837	The full surface is in `gpui-kit.d.ts` next to this file.
838	
839	### The `herdr` module
840	
841	All of it is in `herdr.d.ts`. In short:
842	
843	- Live data: `spaces()` (each with its tabs, status, name, named, folder,
844	  machine, branch), `machines()` (name, null for this computer; layout:
845	  `loading`, `ready`, or `unavailable` on this connection; loading ends on
846	  the first read even if it fails, and offline machines are unavailable),
847	  `agents()` (status, app, space, tab, focused), `terminals()`
848	  (every core terminal), `focused()`, `layout()`, `theme()` (every color by
849	  name: background (the terminals', cards), canvas (behind cards), chrome
850	  (sidebars, bars), surface, popover, raised, hover, selected, border,
851	  input (a stronger border), foreground, muted, dim, accent,
852	  accent_foreground, solid and solid_foreground (a primary button),
853	  selection, working, blocked, done, idle, unknown, ansi0..15; light and
854	  dark themes name the same ones), `settings()` (with `dark`: the
855	  appearance now), `keys()`, `commands()` (every app
856	  command, its arguments and what it does), `layouts()` (the layout names).
857	  `focused().agent` is the agent an agent block shows.
858	  `focused().space`/`tab` describe the current window context. With a layout terminal
859	  block focused, `pane` and `shown` are null; `terminal` and `cwd` describe that block,
860	  not its source pane. Check `focused()?.pane` before offering pane controls.
861	  `panes()` still lists only model panes; none is focused while a terminal block is.
862	  For composition navigation: `run("pane.focus", {terminal: nextAddress})`.
863	  Terminal copy/paste and implicit right-click routing follow the focused block.
864	- Floating: `placement()` (null unless this copy floats).
865	- Act: `run(command, args)`.
866	- Overlays: `openOverlay({ mod, props, kind: "dialog" | "popup" | "window", width, height, at, frame })`
867	  returns an id; the mod gets `props().overlay` and closes itself with
868	  `closeOverlay(id)`; Esc closes the top dialog or popup. `frame: "none"`
869	  drops Herdr's border, corners and shadow so the mod draws its own.
870	  `notify({ title, body, level, icon, timeout })` posts a notification, drawn by the `toast` mod.
871	- Windows (`kind: "window"`): stay open until closed, over the layout and
872	  under dialogs; a press the mod doesn't stop drags it (stop it on your
873	  controls, like a title bar's buttons), it stays where dropped, and the one
874	  pressed last is on top. Sized by content unless `width`/`height`; at `at`
875	  or centered. `key: "name"` remembers its spot (opening that key again
876	  replaces it); `keep: true` with a key reopens it on the next start. A
877	  layout switch closes windows; kept ones come back with their layout.
878	  A window can hold a layout, terminals too: a terminal keeps its presses
879	  (selecting text), so give it a mod block to drag by, a title bar:
880	  `openOverlay({ kind: "window", key: "t7", width: 600, height: 400, layout: { type: "column", children: [{ type: "block", size: { px: 28 }, content: { mod: "my-titlebar" } }, { type: "block", content: { terminal: "t7" } }] } })`.
881	- Machine: `exec(cmd, args, { cwd, on })` (the user's real environment; use this,
882	  not `process.run`; `on: space.machine` runs there, omitted means local).
883	  It rejects if the program cannot start or the machine cannot be reached.
884	  `hc(args)` (`hc read <t>` gives a terminal's text),
885	  `home()`, `appHome()`, `playSound("done" | "blocked" | file)`.
886	  `knownAgents({ on })`: the agents people can start (programs.json's
887	  `run`), most picked first, each `installed` or not there (asked of the
888	  shell agents start in); start one with `argv: agent.run`.
889	  `pickFolder({ prompt })`: the system's folder picker (here only),
890	  resolves with the folder or null.
891	- Files: `readTextFile(path, { on })` (here, or on that machine),
892	  `writeTextFile(path, text, expected)` (here only), and
893	  `watchFolder(dir)` (here only; poll a remote space's folder): resolves with the changed paths the next time anything
894	  under `dir` changes (none missed between calls), so a file tree, a board
895	  or a git panel stays live without polling:
896	  `cx.spawn(async (cx) => { for (;;) { await watchFolder(dir); this.reload(); cx.notify(); } })`.
897	- `notify({ ..., action: { name, args } })`: the toast runs the command when clicked.
898	- This copy: `props()`, `shared(key)` / `setShared(key, value)` (every mod
899	  sees it; setting re-renders all), `nextCommand()` (key commands for this
900	  mod: `cx.spawn(async (cx) => { for (;;) { const c = await nextCommand(); …; cx.notify(); } })`).
901	
902	Mods are trusted code: commands and network access (including `fetch`) are unrestricted.
903	Other built-ins: `localStorage` (per mod copy), `console.log`, `fetch`,
904	`import * as fs from "fs/promises"` (read in home, write under `~/.config/herdr-app`).
905	
906	## herdr-core (`hc`)
907	
908	`herdr-app --skill` prints the manual for driving this window;
909	`hc --skill` prints the manual for running and coordinating programs and agents,
910	including a small herdr-core skill you can install with the user's permission.
911	`herdr-app commands` lists app commands and arguments without needing an open window.
912	
913	- `hc ls --json`, `hc read t3 --lines 50`, `hc run --json --cwd <dir> --label k=v -- <cmd>`,
914	  `hc label t3 k=v`, `hc send t3 "text"`, `hc wait t3`. `hc --help` for all.

919	## Keep in mind
920	
921	- A task's `cx` belongs to the copy that started it: `cx.notify()` redraws
922	  that copy, even when another copy woke it (a shared promise).
923	- One mod per idea. Don't edit `AGENTS.md` or the `.d.ts` files (the app
